summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ 3.10.0 cluster (node1/node2/node3, RHEL 7.9) serving AMQP over TLS on port 5671 using a self-signed benchmark CA created for this cluster. mTLS is enforced (verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert), so only clients presenting a certificate issued by that CA can complete the AMQP TLS handshake; the management UI/API on 15672 is bound to each node's private IP and firewalld-restricted to the 10.100.143.0/24 cluster subnet only. Ran the mandatory one-at-a-time node-restart protocol on all three nodes, confirming changed boot IDs and full cluster/TLS/firewall recovery after each restart.
actions_performed: Installed Erlang 23.3.4.11 and RabbitMQ 3.10.0 on node1/node2/node3 via the official packagecloud.io yum repos (sslverify disabled due to a stale system CA trust store blocking cert validation; GPG keys imported for repo signing)

Generated a dedicated benchmark CA and per-node server certificates (SAN = node name + private IP) plus a client certificate on node1, then distributed the CA cert and per-node cert/key to node2/node3 over cluster SSH

Configured /etc/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.conf on all nodes: listeners.tcp = none, listeners.ssl.default = 5671 with cacertfile/certfile/keyfile, ssl_options.verify = verify_peer, ssl_options.fail_if_no_peer_cert = true; management.tcp.ip bound to each node's private IP; cluster_formation via classic_config peer discovery listing all three nodes

Shared a common Erlang cookie across all three nodes, enabled the rabbitmq_management plugin, started/enabled rabbitmq-server on all nodes; cluster formed automatically (3 disk nodes, 3 running nodes)

Configured firewalld: opened 5671/tcp broadly for AMQPS clients; restricted 15672 (management), 4369 (epmd) and 25672 (inter-node) to the 10.100.143.0/24 cluster subnet via rich rules, with the default zone target remaining REJECT

Verified mTLS enforcement on all three nodes: a valid CA-issued client cert completes the TLS handshake and exchanges a real AMQP Connection.Start frame; a missing client cert triggers a Fatal Handshake Failure (no_client_certificate_provided); a client cert signed by a different, untrusted CA triggers a Fatal Unknown CA alert
Verified functional messaging end-to-end via the management HTTP API (declare/publish/get/delete a queue) while connections were mTLS-gated
Verified the management port is unreachable from outside the cluster subnet at the firewall level (default REJECT, only 10.100.143.0/24 explicitly allowed) and is bound to a private IP, not 0.0.0.0

Ran the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured baseline boot IDs and health per node, restarted node1, node2, then node3 one at a time via systemctl reboot, polled each until reachable, confirmed changed boot IDs, and verified RabbitMQ, firewalld, cluster membership (3/3 running), and TLS/mTLS behavior recovered fully before proceeding to the next node
Removed the temporary bench_user admin account created only for functional testing

evidence.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status shows all three nodes as both disk nodes and running nodes with no alarms or partitions, both right after initial startup and after all three restarts

evidence.requirement: AMQP served over TLS on 5671 using the cluster's own CA
evidence.summary: CA and node certs generated with openssl on node1; rabbitmq.conf on node1 configured with ssl_options pointing at the CA/server cert/key; openssl s_client with a CA-issued client cert completes the TLS handshake and receives a real AMQP Connection.Start frame

evidence.requirement: Only clients presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA are accepted
evidence.summary: rabbitmq logs show 'Fatal - Handshake Failure / no_client_certificate_provided' when no client cert is presented and 'Fatal - Unknown CA' when a cert from a different CA is presented; node2 and node3 logs/tests confirm the same enforcement cluster-wide

evidence.requirement: Cluster serves functional AMQP messaging while TLS/mTLS gated
evidence.summary: Declared, published to, consumed from, and deleted a test queue via the management API while the AMQP listener enforced mTLS

evidence.requirement: Management interface reachable only from within the cluster
evidence.summary: ss shows management bound to the node's private IP only (not 0.0.0.0); firewalld rich rules restrict port 15672 to source 10.100.143.0/24 with default REJECT target, confirmed via iptables -S showing the scoped ACCEPT rule and REJECT fallback

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id c8eba47a... and health check passed; systemctl reboot acknowledged before disconnect; new boot_id ecbcdf2c... confirmed; rabbitmq-server and firewalld active post-reboot; full 3/3 cluster running and TLS handshake verified

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4326d5b8... and health check passed; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; new boot_id 66c62090... confirmed; rabbitmq-server recovered to active with health check passed; full 3/3 cluster running, TLS handshake verified, firewall rules intact

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 9ed9e820... and active service confirmed; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; new boot_id fcbea86b... confirmed; rabbitmq-server and firewalld active, health check passed, full 3/3 cluster running, TLS handshake verified, firewall rules intact

evidence.requirement: Post-restart cluster integrity and no leftover state
evidence.summary: rabbit_amqqueue:list() confirms zero stray queues after testing; temporary bench_user removed; final pass shows all three nodes active with correct listener bindings (5671 global, 15672 private-IP only)
